zusammenfassung: This week AI improves where it makes the work context more controllable. Claude Fable 5.1 combines text work with a relevant retention architecture; Atlas turns space and camera into controllable design parameters. HubSpot AEO, Articos and Ritto show three different paths: measurability, hypothesis testing and demonstrated automation. The productive question is not "What can the AI do?" but "What can I clearly limit, check and take responsibility for?"
highlights: Claude Fable 5.1 (8.7/10): higher performance, cheaper cache reads and customer-controlled retention bring text AI closer to controllable knowledge work.
Trend: value does not come from more AI output but from control over data flow, spatial context, sources and approvals.
Rule of thumb: pilot beta tools only with approved test data, reversible steps and measurable quality criteria.
trend: AI quality increasingly comes from controllability: data flow, spatial context, sources and human approvals become the real product feature.
